purpose: Prevent original-edition volume numbering, later reprint numbering, and acquisition status from being conflated during Mundarica completeness auditing.

findings.statement: Current external bibliographic evidence confirms an original Government Printing Volume 13 published in 1941 and secondary catalogue evidence for a Government Printing set described as Vol. 1-13. This does not by itself prove that every historical issue/part maps one-to-one to thirteen physical volumes.

sources.observed_metadata: Encyclopaedia Mundarica, Volume 13; Johann Hoffmann and Arthur van Emelen; Superintendent government printing, Bihar and Orissa; 1941
Bookseller catalogue describes Encyclopaedia Mundarica; Vol. 1-13; Patna: Superintendent, Government Printing; 1950

findings.statement: A later Gyan Publishing House series is explicitly catalogued as 'In 16 Volumes'; Volume 16 is independently represented by ISBN 9788121203227. Therefore XIV-XVI may be valid reprint-series volume identifiers even if historical Government Printing catalogues are organized differently.

sources.observed_metadata: Encyclopaedia Mundarica: In 16 Volumes, Volume 13; Gyan Publishing House; 2009
Encyclopaedia Mundarica Vol.16th; ISBN 978-81-212-0322-7; 2009; Gyan Publishing House/Repro India listing

audit_rule: Do not mark XIV-XVI missing from the historical edition merely because a modern 16-volume reprint exists, and do not mark a historical slot complete from a modern reprint locator without edition-level mapping. Track edition, physical volume/part, identifier, scan provenance and page range separately.
completion_effect: No machine VERIFIED COMPLETE state changes from this reconciliation alone.
next_required_checks: Obtain authoritative library/publisher table-of-contents or catalog records for the complete original Government Printing sequence.
Obtain authoritative metadata for Gyan reprint Volumes XIV, XV and XVI, including ISBNs and contents/page spans.
Establish an explicit original-edition-to-reprint mapping before using modern volume numbers in historical completeness metrics.
